articles.title: Spain's Canary Islands flooded by thousands of migrants as country declares emergency
articles.summary: Spain's Canary Islands processed over 2,200 migrants in two days as violent protests over housing costs and skyrocketing rents erupted nationwide.
articles.body:
Thousands of migrants flooded Spain's Canary Islands this weekend as the nation's government remains under a migration emergency.

The Canary Islands have received the brunt of migration from West Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa in recent months. Authorities there processed over 2,200 migrants in just two days, all arriving in dinghies and makeshift boats.

One flotilla of 14 boats landed on the island of El Hierro carrying 1,324 people. The island's Spanish population is just 12,000.

The Spanish government declared an emergency over the archipelago last week. The latest surge comes just months after tens of thousands of migrants crossed into Spain's North African territory of Cueta in July.

The country also faced internal unrest this month after a general strike turned violent last week and rioters began clashing with police, setting fires and bashing storefronts in hotspots across the country.

Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona , where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles.

The violence erupted as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living.

Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, The Associated Press reported.

The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid.

Both the migration and housing crises are expected to play a major role in Spain's Nov. 29 parliamentary elections.

Fox News' Jasmine Baehr and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Aarón Escandell desvela cómo trabaja Raúl en el Oviedo: "Es muy exigente"
articles.standfirst: El portero destaca el trato directo del entrenador y explica qué les pide en el campo tras su primera semana
articles.summary: El portero destaca el trato directo del entrenador y explica qué les pide en el campo tras su primera semana
articles.body: "Es una persona muy cercana. Le gusta el contacto directo con los jugadores". Así describe Aarón Escandell a Raúl González Blanco tras su primera semana al frente del Real Oviedo. El guardameta explicó que el técnico está pendiente de cómo se encuentra cada futbolista y que "se guía mucho por las sensaciones de los jugadores". En cuanto empieza la sesión, sube el listón. "Es muy exigente. Le gusta que, una vez que empecemos a trabajar, demos el cien por cien". Escandell contó que el equipo ha "acumulado durante la semana mucha carga" y que al nuevo entrenador le gusta dedicar tiempo a trabajar sobre el césped. "Todo facilidades, todo muy bien, cero problemas", resumió sobre esos primeros días. El portero también habló de la disposición del vestuario en el primer proyecto de Raúl como técnico en el fútbol profesional. "Nosotros también tenemos que apoyarle y ayudarle". ¿Y cómo quiere Raúl que juegue su Oviedo? "Nos pide que seamos valientes. Tiene muy claro cómo quiere que seamos", explicó Escandell. La idea, detalló, pasa por "ser protagonistas con balón" y situar el bloque "muy alto", tanto en ataque como en defensa. El guardameta aprecia "un par de matices" respecto a lo que ya hacía el equipo y espera que se vean con el paso de las semanas. "Durante este tiempo se va a ir viendo lo que él quiere", dijo. A la plantilla le toca llevar al partido lo que trabaja en los entrenamientos. El estreno ante el Girona dejó una derrota en el Carlos Tartiere después de que el Oviedo se adelantara. "Hacemos lo más difícil, que es ponerte por delante de un rival que está ahí arriba, y después en prácticamente diez minutos encajamos dos goles", repasó el portero. "No fue nuestro mejor partido en casa". Escandell puso el acento en los "pequeños detalles" que impidieron sumar y explicó que ya habían repasado lo sucedido con Raúl y el resto del equipo. El guardameta también espera que las nuevas consignas se noten cerca del área rival. "Creo que ahora seremos un poco más verticales y seremos más valientes de cara al ataque". Ante la falta de gol, defendió que el trabajo empieza mucho antes del remate. "Para que los delanteros metan goles, tenemos que llegar como bloque y crear". Y en su área se aplicó la misma exigencia. "Soy el primer autocrítico", dijo al recordar cuánto le duele no dejar la portería a cero. El próximo examen será en Córdoba. Escandell espera que el Oviedo pueda presionar arriba y discutirle el balón a un rival que, a su juicio, hace mucho daño si encuentra espacio y tiempo. "Si le hacemos el partido incómodo y nosotros con balón estamos acertados y le quitamos la posesión, pienso que será donde le podemos hacer daño".

articles.title: Jon Ander Ulazia, presidente del Eibar a todos los efectos
articles.standfirst: Amaia Gorostiza presentó su dimisión como presidenta y renunció a su condición de consejera y el Consejo aprobó el nombramiento de su sucesor
articles.summary: Amaia Gorostiza presentó su dimisión como presidenta y renunció a su condición de consejera y el Consejo aprobó el nombramiento de su sucesor
articles.body: Amaia Gorostiza ya es historia del Eibar. La empresaria eibarresa se despidió el domingo de su cargo como presidenta en el choque que enfrentó al equipo ante el Cádiz. Muchas de las personas más importantes que han pasado por el club durante su mandato estuvieron cerca suyo en el último encuentro al frente del club. Desde José Luis Mendilibar hasta Gaizka Garitano, pasando por otras figuras como Beñat San José, Fran Garagarza, Mikel Martija o Arkaitz Lakanbra. El domingo fue su despedida oficial, aunque fue ayer cuando presentó su dimisión como presidenta y también renunció a su condición de consejera en el Consejo de Administración celebrado en Ipurua. Un acto en el que también se aprobó el nombramiento de Jon Ander Ulazia como nuevo presidente. El abogado eibarrés comparecerá este miércoles en Ipurua, pero ya es desde ayer por la tarde la máxima institución armera. Ulazia no es un desconocido en el mundo del fútbol. Todo lo contrario. Lleva 14 años como directivo, fue Consejero Delegado del club entre 2019 y 2023, siendo una pieza fundamental en el proyecto armero y también cuenta con un papel relevante dentro de la industria, hasta el punto de ser vicepresidente de la Liga. Un apasionado del fútbol, que siente el Eibar dentro y que lleva tiempo preparándose para asumir este reto. Gorostiza siempre tuvo claro que su relevo natural tenía que ser Ulazia, un nombramiento que ha sido muy bien recibido por la afición armera. El salto de Jon Ander a la presidencia es una apuesta continuista y que tampoco cambiará el funcionamiento del club. Será la cabeza visible, aunque las decisiones seguirán tomándose de forma conjunta y en consenso, como ha sucedido en la última década con Gorostiza. Licenciado en Derecho con Especialidad en Economía por la Universidad de Deusto, Ulazia destaca por su cercanía y por ser un tipo natural, pero además tiene conocimiento sobre el fútbol, sobre el funcionamiento de la industria y sobre cómo debe gestionarse un club en todos los sentidos, gracias, entre otras cosas, a los cuatro años que estuvo como Consejero Delegado. Mañana se presentará ante los medios, pero su mandato, como mínimo hasta 2027, ya está en marcha

articles.title: Arch Manning will participate in Texas' senior day festivities before Arkansas game
articles.summary: Manning is in his fourth season with the Longhorns.
articles.body:
Saturday's game against Arkansas could be Arch Manning's final home game as a Texas Longhorn.

Manning, a fourth-year player, is participating in the school's senior day festivities ahead of the game. When asked about it Monday, Manning had a straightforward answer.

"I'm a senior, so I'm doing it," he said via the AP.

However, Manning's senior day participation doesn't mean much. Even without the NCAA's new five-for-five rule, Manning would have the ability to return to school in 2027. While Manning is about to finish his fourth season of college football, he'd be able to play next year anyway if he chooses to eschew the NFL because he played in just two games as a redshirt in 2023.

Manning, who said he didn't want to discuss his future Monday, has three clear options next season. He can return to Texas, head to the NFL or transfer to another school. Manning's draft status will be fascinating after an uneven-at-times season. He threw three interceptions against LSU before throwing the game-winning touchdown pass. And his late interceptions against Oklahoma led to the Sooners' Red River Rivalry win.

Manning could still be a first-round pick. Especially in a quarterback class that doesn't have much clarity.

If he stays in school — whether at Texas or elsewhere — he'll probably be one of the highest-paid quarterbacks in the country. A Manning transfer would also likely be the most talked-about player move of the NIL era.

But that's an option that's not worth discussing seriously at the moment. A win Saturday almost ensures Texas will be in the College Football Playoff. And given the way that the 2026 season has unfolded, we aren't discounting Texas' title chances if it makes the 12-team field even if the Longhorns haven't consistently looked like a complete football team.

articles.title: OFFSIDE | £2.27 billion, zero league titles: How Manchester United became football's most expensive 'tragedy'
articles.summary: Hello and welcome to another edition of Offside.
articles.body: Hello and welcome to another edition of Offside. There’s a line in the eminently forgettable The Godfather Part III – whose only redemption was the Dimitar Berbatov lookalike Andy Garcia playing Vincent Mancini, the illegitimate son of Sonny Corleone – in which Al Pacino’s Michael Corleone says, “Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in.” Joey Tribbiani immortalised the line in the Friends episode where he gets to play Al Pacino’s posterior. And that’s how Manchester United fans have felt after every managerial hiring and firing in the post-Fergie era.The latest manager to have been handed that poisoned chalice is Mauricio Pochettino, who – to borrow a phrase from an articulate social media user – has been handpicked from the United States men’s team to improve United’s state. Now, Pochettino is a talented manager – any man who can take Tottenham Hotspur to a Champions League final is entitled to the benefit of the doubt. But improving United’s state is easier said than done. Since the great Scot hung up his overcoat, the Panglossian optimism that used to greet every managerial appointment has given way to a Kafkaesque certitude of grief.Last week, Offside argued that one shouldn’t judge Cristiano Ronaldo’s career by the sheer numbers. This week, we are going to put on our bean counters’ hats and look at what Manchester United got for their money.What £2.27 billion buys youSince Sir Alex Ferguson bid adieu, the Red Devils have spent over £2 billion on players, and perhaps only Bruno Fernandes can be considered a roaring success. He could walk into some of Ferguson’s best teams, though Messrs Keane, Giggs, Scholes and Cantona would frown upon his on-pitch whining.After David Moyes took the champions to seventh, United opened their chequebook for Louis van Gaal, who brought in Ángel Di María (£59.7 million) and an 18-year-old Anthony Martial (£36 million initially).José Mourinho followed with Paul Pogba (£89 million), whom United had previously allowed to leave for free, and Romelu Lukaku (£75 million).Ole Gunnar Solskjaer added Harry Maguire (£80 million), Jadon Sancho (£73 million) and Cristiano Ronaldo (£12.8 million initially), whose return produced one epochal Peter Drury commentary, a few goals and a bust-up that ended with his contract being mutually terminated.Erik ten Hag then signed Antony (£81 million), whose spinning abilities were considerably more impressive than his footballing ones, and Rasmus Højlund (up to £72 million). Of that expensive collection, only Maguire and, to a certain extent, Pogba could be considered successes.The telling comparison is with Ferguson, whose net spending in his final eight seasons was £153.2 million, or £19.2 million annually, yielding five Premier League titles and three Champions League finals, winning one. In the 13 completed seasons since, United have paid £2.27 billion for players, received just £586 million from sales and spent a net £1.68 billion, or £129.3 million annually.These are cash payments, including instalments, not headline transfer fees. In the post-Fergie doomsday, average annual net spending increased nearly sevenfold, but league titles fell from five to zero. A club that never finished below second in Ferguson’s final eight seasons fell to 15th and currently sits 18th.United recovered roughly 55 pence for each pound spent under Ferguson, against 26 pence since his retirement. Nothing illustrates the madness better than Pogba, who left for nothing, returned for £89 million and left for nothing again.The price of hiring and firing managersIf the transfer strategy bordered on the farcical, the managerial merry-go-round has been even worse. A Telegraph calculation reported by Reuters puts the bill for hiring and dismissing managers, coaches and senior staff at over £108 million since Ferguson retired, excluding salaries. The departures of Moyes (£4.9 million), Van Gaal (£8.4 million), Mourinho (£19.6 million), Solskjaer (£9.1 million) and Ten Hag (£10.4 million) were followed by United paying Sporting about £9.2 million for Rúben Amorim, then £8.2 million on his departure and restructuring.The latest act was handing Michael Carrick a two-year contract in May 2026, then sacking him less than six months later. Settlements for him and his staff are estimated to cost at least £5 million, while releasing Pochettino from US Soccer is expected to cost around £7.4 million. That is £12.4 million on another reset, when United could have approached Pochettino after the World Cup, before he extended his US contract in August, instead of giving Carrick the permanent gig without a senior out-and-out goalscorer, cover for Luke Shaw or anyone to fill the void left by Casemiro.Each manager inherited his predecessor’s expensive mistakes, received money to make his own and got a golden handshake on being sacked.The debt that survived FergusonNow, no financial analysis of United makes sense without talking about the debt with which the Glazers’ leveraged takeover in 2005 saddled the club. Ferguson, whose high-horse issues did play a part in that particular saddling, managed to win despite those constraints. In his final eight seasons, United paid £495.5 million in cash interest, more than they spent buying players. After his retirement, United paid a further £347.7 million in cash interest and £156.2 million in shareholder dividends, a combined £503.9 million.Gross borrowing rose from £389.2 million in June 2013 to approximately £689 million in June 2026, against £67.2 million in cash. A September estimate of £1.15 billion also included £375 million in unpaid transfers, a liability distinct from bank debt.Record revenue, record absurdityDespite their league position and lack of European football, the United brand has proved resilient. Revenue rose from £363.2 million in Ferguson’s final season to a club-record £677.6 million in 2025/26, achieved without European football, and yet United recorded their seventh consecutive annual loss, taking the cumulative deficit to £444 million. That season produced £22.6 million in operating profit, but £69.6 million in net finance costs turned it into a £47 million pre-tax loss and, after a tax credit, a £43 million net loss.Amortisation of £211.8 million reflected past player purchases: the manager may have left, but his transfer decisions keep appearing in the accounts.Enter Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS, whose solution to this expensive chaos would have gladdened Scrooge’s heart. United’s staff headcount fell from 1,127 in June 2024 to 805 in June 2026. Sir Alex Ferguson’s paid ambassadorial arrangement was also ended, and Ratcliffe showed the same disdain for free staff lunches as he does for immigrants, ending them for staff members.No wonder fans are chanting that Ratcliffe can stick the new stadium up his ******, while the club is selling Old Trafford turf for £125 apiece.The contrast with the erstwhile “noisy neighbours” could hardly be more delicious. Across Manchester, City were found guilty of financial doping involving more than £900 million in artificially inflated revenues and reduced costs, a verdict they are appealing. City's financial chicanery at least produced trophies; United's billions produced no league titles.City cooked the books to win on the grass; United closed the kitchen and ended up selling the grass.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 Panic Meter: Trey McBride's ceiling will be limited if Cardinals' offense continues to struggle
articles.summary: Ray Garvin highlights the panic level for players and situations in fantasy football going into Week 11.
articles.body:
This week, I'm starting with the team that might surprise you — because I've reached the point where there's nothing left to panic about.

New England totaled 151 net yards in a 35-10 loss to Detroit. Drake Maye exited on the opening drive, and Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards in relief. The passing game already offered little margin for error.

The bigger concern is Maye's ankle injury. Reports have raised the possibility that he could miss the remainder of the season , and Mike Vrabel doesn't expect him to be available immediately after the Week 11 bye. A season-ending absence isn't confirmed, but the fantasy playoff implications are serious.

That brings us to A.J. Brown. He's dealing with injuries of his own, and the temptation will be to put him right back into lineups whenever he's cleared. The numbers don't support it. Brown has 11 catches for 128 yards and no touchdowns in four games with Maye. DeVito doesn't improve that outlook.

Hunter Henry has a slightly different argument. Tight end has been a difficult position all season, and an inexperienced quarterback leaning on a veteran tight end makes sense in theory. But Henry's two catches against Detroit both came on the opening drive with Maye. He didn't record a reception from DeVito. He's a desperation option.

So, are Maye and Brown droppable in seasonal redraft leagues?

Maye is approaching that point, if the injury timeline rules him out for the fantasy playoffs, particularly in leagues without an available IR spot. Brown is more dependent on league size and replacement options. In a standard 10- or 12-team league, moving on is reasonable if the waiver wire offers someone with a clearer path to usable production.

There's no obvious quarterback rescue coming for this passing game.

Panic Meter: NO PANIC. Expectations have already been reset. New England isn't an offense to chase for fantasy production until the situation changes.

Chris Olave, WR, New Orleans Saints — SOME PANIC

Four targets for Chris Olave against Carolina. That's the number that stands out.

He finished with three catches for 30 yards, just one week after catching seven passes for 98 yards on 12 targets against Cleveland. The Cleveland game broke a streak of three straight outings under 60 yards.

Meanwhile, Jordyn Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards. The question is how Tyler Shough is distributing the ball, not whether Tyson has taken over.

Olave had reached double-digit targets in six of his first eight games. That volume helped offset the inconsistency of the Saints' passing attack and gave him a dependable path to fantasy points, even when the offense struggled. Fewer targets would widen his weekly range of outcomes.

One week doesn't establish a permanent shift, but Tyson's involvement is worth tracking. New Orleans doesn't consistently generate enough passing production to make an unexpected four-target afternoon easy to absorb.

Olave should remain in starting lineups. He still has the ability to produce strong fantasy weeks, and a single low-volume performance doesn't outweigh his season-long role.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. The concern isn't Olave's talent. It's whether the target advantage that has supported his production is becoming less reliable.

Kyren Williams, RB, Los Angeles Rams — SOME PANIC+

If you've watched the Rams' backfield recently, Blake Corum's explosiveness has been difficult to miss. Sean McVay has noticed too, praising Corum's twitch and explosiveness after his 100-yard performance against Arizona.

From Weeks 8 through 10, Corum rushed for 231 yards on 39 carries, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt. Kyren Williams totaled 124 yards on 43 carries, just 2.9 per attempt. Corum generated nearly twice the yardage on fewer opportunities.

Against Arizona, Corum finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. Williams managed 23 rushing yards on 12 attempts. The Rams won comfortably, but the backs had very different afternoons.

Williams still matters to this offense. His work in pass protection and the passing game gives him a role that doesn't disappear just because Corum has been more efficient on the ground. The question is how much of the rushing workload he can retain while Corum keeps producing.

There's no confirmed depth-chart change, but the old workload assumptions deserve another look. Corum has given the coaching staff a reason to keep him involved.

The Week 11 bye gives Los Angeles time to evaluate its rotation. Watch the touch distribution coming out of it rather than assuming the old split automatically returns.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC+. Williams is still a viable fantasy starter, but his weekly ceiling is getting harder to project with Corum earning more work.

Sam LaPorta, TE, Detroit Lions — SOME PANIC

Detroit scored 35 points against New England, and Sam LaPorta caught one pass for 16 yards. That sums up the problem. The Lions offense can function at a high level without LaPorta making much of an impact in the box score.

Over his last four games, LaPorta has nine receptions for 99 yards and no touchdowns on 16 targets. The opportunities haven't been there. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown remain central to the offense, and Detroit has enough ways to score without featuring its tight end.

For fantasy managers, that leaves LaPorta heavily dependent on touchdowns. It's a difficult way to operate at an already volatile position, especially when he hasn't found the end zone in four straight games.

There are reasons to be patient. Detroit routinely creates scoring opportunities, so a usage increase could turn into a productive week quickly. The problem is identifying when that usage is actually coming.

LaPorta shouldn't be viewed as an unquestioned starter based only on the quality of his offense. Matchups and available alternatives matter more now than they did earlier in the season.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. Detroit's scoring potential keeps the upside alive, but it hasn't protected LaPorta's weekly floor.

Trey McBride, TE, Arizona Cardinals — SOME PANIC

Trey McBride caught every pass thrown his way Sunday. There were only five.

He finished with five receptions for 37 yards against the Rams, but Arizona's overall performance tells the bigger story. The Cardinals ran 34 offensive plays, earned six first downs and failed on all six third-down attempts.

Carson Beck threw for 108 yards with two interceptions in his first NFL start. Arizona scored six points and has managed just nine over its last two games. That's not enough sustained offense to support reliable fantasy production, regardless of how good McBride is at earning targets.

When drives end after a few snaps, even a strong target share means limited opportunities. McBride didn't lose his role. Arizona simply couldn't keep its offense on the field.

Total Panic would be premature. Beck drew a difficult Rams matchup in his debut, and one start isn't enough to determine what the passing game will look like over the final stretch. Kansas City is next, so the evaluation won't get easier, but the rookie deserves another opportunity before his impact on McBride is treated as settled.

The comparison with LaPorta is useful. Detroit can score without feeding LaPorta. Arizona needs McBride involved, but its offense hasn't been able to sustain drives. Same position, very different paths to disappointing fantasy results.

McBride should remain in starting lineups. Very few tight ends combine his talent with his share of their team's passing opportunities. The production may be inconsistent until Arizona improves, but benching him would create a different kind of risk.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. Give Beck another start. If Arizona continues to struggle to move the chains, McBride's ceiling will be limited by the offense around him.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 11 lineups
articles.summary: Fantasy analyst Fred Zinkie highlights some backup RBs who could crack starting lineups in Week 11.
articles.body:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy teams to victory in Week 11. Players are ranked in order of their Week 11 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

Two things were clear when the 49ers hung 46 points on the Cowboys. First, Christian McCaffrey is at the top of his game and the clear focal point of the offense. Second, even with McCaffrey having a heavy workload, there is still room for Black to have a significant role. The rookie has logged at least 11 carries in each of the past three games and has found the end zone twice during that stretch. While San Francisco is set for a challenging Week 11 showdown with a stifling Vikings defense, there may be no stopping one of the hottest offenses in football. Black is a flex option each week and an RB2 option in a Week 11 schedule that includes six teams on a bye.

Gainwell went into the Bucs' bye week on a high note, having averaged 101 yards from scrimmage in the previous three games. The 27-year-old is clearly second fiddle to Bucky Irving, who has been one of the top fantasy assets this season. But there are plenty of carries to go around in Tampa's run-heavy offense that leads the NFL in yards on the ground. They will likely remain conservative with play-calling when they visit the high-octane Lions in Week 11.

Managers who dropped McGowan when Jonathan Taylor remained with the Colts past the trade deadline were surely second-guessing their decision when McGowan tallied 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in a Week 10 win over the Dolphins. While facing Miami is one of the easiest matchups, McGowan is far from a one-game wonder, having averaged 5.8 yards on 34 carries over the past four weeks. After trading their top receivers and watching Daniel Jones struggle throughout the season, the Colts could copy teams like the 49ers and Buccaneers by running their offense through multiple RBs.

The bad news: Kamara touched the ball just five times in a Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The good news: he turned those touches into two touchdowns. The 31-year-old will continue to have a role in the offense, as Travis Etienne Jr. and Audric Estimé did little with their Week 10 opportunities. Kamara is averaging three catches per game, which gives him additional value in PPR leagues for a possible Week 11 shootout in Chicago.

Woody Marks will miss Thursday Night Football after leaving the Week 10 loss to the Browns with a concussion. David Montgomery may be ready to return for a favorable matchup against the Colts, but he hasn't played since Oct. 11 and may not be ready for a heavy workload. The Texans are double-digit favorites against a defense that has been repeatedly burned by opposing RBs, and Houston could spend the fourth quarter grinding out rushing yards to put the game away. Demercado is a candidate to fill that role after tallying 13 carries in the past two weeks. And if Montgomery remains out, Demercado becomes the starter and jumps at least two spots higher on this list.

Derrick Henry may be reaching the end of his illustrious career. The future Hall of Famer averaged 1.0 yards per carry against a mediocre Chargers defense in Week 10, which was the fourth time in the past five weeks that his average per carry fell below 3.5. Hill has managed to break a couple long runs this season and is averaging 6.8 yards per carry. He has also caught at least three passes in each of his past five games, including a five-catch game in Week 10. Hill should remain involved in Week 11, when the Ravens face a Panthers defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to RBs.

Although he wasn't especially effective, Washington led the Raiders with 23 rushing yards in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Starter Ashton Jeanty once again dominated receiving targets, while Washington has led the team in rushing yards in four of their past five games, and his 3.9 yards per carry this season tops Jeanty's 3.2 mark. Washington should earn 8-10 carries but a lack of passing-game involvement gives him a low ceiling for a challenging Week 11 matchup in Denver.

Anyone who has watched Saquon Barkley in recent weeks knows that he is not fully healthy. The generational talent lacks his usually explosive burst, and it doesn't help that the Eagles are missing multiple starters while sitting at 2-7. Bigsby is expected to return from injured reserve for a Week 11 matchup against the Steelers, and he should immediately slot ahead of Elijah Mitchell on the depth chart. Bigsby could get 5-10 carries in that game and is worth stashing in the event that the Eagles eventually shut Barkley down for their meaningless late-season games.

Bhayshul Tuten was used heavily in a 40-point explosion in Week 10, carrying the ball 26 times and catching three passes. Rodriguez had an especially quiet day, with five yards on four carries. Truthfully, if there were fewer than six teams on a bye in Week 11, he would likely fall off this list. But with a dearth of alternatives, he's a TD-dependent flex option in deep leagues for a challenging matchup against a Giants defense that has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

Davis has had almost no impact on Buffalo's offense this season, totaling just 92 total yards over nine games played. Most weeks, Ty Johnson would be the Bills backup who could dent deep-league rosters, as he has caught 18 passes for 214 yards. But the Bills are massive favorites for a Week 11 home game against the 1-8 Dolphins, with the point spread sitting around 16-17 points. If the team builds a massive lead, Davis is the most likely candidate to receive plenty of second-half carries.

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 10 but are an injury away from having significant value.

articles.title: El Caso Líbero visto para sentencia: finaliza el juicio y el futuro del Granada, en juego
articles.standfirst: El club nazarí, junto al resto de acusados, se enfrenta a una multa millonaria
articles.summary: El club nazarí, junto al resto de acusados, se enfrenta a una multa millonaria
articles.body: Mientras el Granada vive un periodo de bonanza en el plano deportivo, tercero en la tabla tras igualar la mejor racha de su historia con seis victorias consecutivas, el club y el granadinismo contienen el aliento a la espera de la sentencia del Caso Líbero, cuyo juicio oral ha concluido en el día de hoy, quedando visto para sentencia, y que podría conllevar una multa millonaria para la entidad, algo que, como ha recordado Javier Aranguren, “sería irremediablemente su fin”. En la presentación del escrito de conclusiones, la Fiscalía y la Abogacía del Estado han afirmado que está acreditado la creación de una “estructura compleja de defraudación tributaria, un plan criminal estructurado desde la toma del control del Granada” por parte de Gino Pozzo, acusado como autor de los hechos, junto a Quique Pina, Jordi Trilles y De la Riva, que se han sentado en el banquillo como cooperadores necesarios. “Gino Pozzo entró en el Granada, se hizo con las ganancias, no tributó y se fue”, ha relatado la Fiscalía, otorgándole al italiano un papel de “parásito” en el club rojiblanco. “Todas las sociedad son gestionados con los fondos de Gino Pozzo, creando un fraude tributario evidente por medio de la simulación”, indican. El plan era claro: no tributar por las ganancias, haciendo salir el dinero en un proceso de simulación, ocultación y disfraz de toda la operativa con la única misión de defraudar a la Hacienda Pública. “Nadie ha tributado por esas ganancias”, aseguran desde el Ministerio Público. Sobre el resto de acusados, la Fiscalía ha calificado a Pina como el “ejecutor” de todo el plan, a De La Riva como el “arquitecto” y a Trilles como otro elemento indispensable para que todo el plan funcionase según lo previsto. Tampoco se ha olvidado la Fiscalía del Granada, para el que, como persona jurídica, se le solicita una multa de 26,9 millones, indicando que en esta ocasión es necesario exigirle responsabilidad penal al considerar evidente que “no había normas de cumplimiento y que se prestó a facilitar toda la trama”, explicaba. El relato ha cambiado de forma drástica cuando ha llegado el turno para los abogados de la defensa, que han ido solicitando de forma sucesiva una sentencia absolutoria para los acusados, para los que se piden penas de 12 años de prisioneros y multas de 27,5 millones, cifra que se eleva hasta los 36,5 en el caso de Gino Pozzo. Según la tesis expuesta por los letrados es intrascendente quién dominaba el Granada, negado que hubiese una economía circular, ha negado la ocultación y también la simulación, exponiendo que todo la ingeniería financiera del Granada era totalmente legal y estaba en conocimiento de la Agencia Tributaria y de La Liga. La defensa del Granada también ha “desvirtuado” todas las tesis acusatorias, pidiendo la absolución para el club respaldándose en todo lo expuesto anteriormente por el resto de abogados defensores. Tras escuchar a todas las partes y con una cantidad ingente de información en su poder, ahora es el turno del juez, que tendrá que dictar sentencia, un fallo que puede marcar el futuro del Granada.

articles.title: Corey Woolfolk coge las riendas del Valencia
articles.standfirst: El hombre fuerte de Pitchwise se reúne en Madrid con Solís y Braulio para trazar la estrategia del club en los próximos meses
articles.summary: El hombre fuerte de Pitchwise se reúne en Madrid con Solís y Braulio para trazar la estrategia del club en los próximos meses
articles.body: Un paso al frente. El nuevo accionista potente del Valencia sigue dando señales de implicación en el proyecto. Pese a que el CSD no ha aprobado aún la operación, y tiene de plazo hasta el 6 de febrero, el fondo americano Pitchwise se ha reunido durante la mañana de hoy con Javier Solís y Braulio Vázquez en Madrid para trazar las líneas del futuro del club a corto y medio plazo. Representados por la figura de Corey Woolfolk los directivos del club se han sentado en una mesa en la capital de España para ponerse cara y dar pasos al frente. Durante la comida se ha abordado el tema deportivo y la situación de urgencia que tiene el equipo para evitar el descenso a segunda división. Corey va a ser el que domine la parte deportiva y era imprescindible tener una toma de contacto real antes de arrancar el trascendental mercado de invierno. De momento, y hasta que se formalice la compra por parte del CSD, no habrá visita de Corey a la ciudad deportiva para conocer a los jugadores y a los empleados del club. La reunión se alargó durante toda la mañana y en ella se estableció la forma de trabajo y de las necesidades para la nueva estructura de ojeadores y formas de actuar en el mercado. No se ha establecido un tope de dinero para fichajes en el mercado de invierno, pero sí se han puesto encima de la mesa el plan de trabajo. Uno de los detalles importantes de la reunión es que no ha estado presente, ni en persona ni de forma telemática, el máximo accionista del club y presidente de la entidad Kiat Lim. En principio se trataba de ponerse cara con el nuevo hombre fuerte en el plano deportivo para trazar el plan de presente y futuro a corto plazo

articles.title: In scathing rebuke of college sports, former Big 12 AD calls NIL system money laundering
articles.summary: Former Iowa State athletic director Jamie Pollard delivered a scorching appraisal of the world he recently left, predicting college sports could be triggerin...
articles.body:
Former Iowa State athletic director Jamie Pollard delivered a scorching appraisal of the world he recently left, predicting college sports could be triggering something akin to the country's "next savings-and-loan crisis" and equating the system that generates NIL payments to players as a money-laundering operation.

"Somehow we're taking money that was supposed to come to our institution and find a way for it to be not given to our institution so we can launder it and create a manufactured NIL deal," Pollard said Wednesday at a seminar held by the college watchdog Knight Commission.

He was referring to the practice many schools use when they work with third parties to broker NIL deals for players. Those deals are allowable constructs that let schools blow past the $21.5 million revenue-sharing cap set by the landmark House settlement that allows college athletes to be paid.

Since the onset of NIL, some sports-focused donations that, in the past, would have gone to an athletic department have been diverted to businesses closely affiliated to the schools. They, in turn, have negotiated the so-called third-party NIL contracts.

Pollard, who spent 21 years as the Cyclones AD before stepping down this fall, decried this process as creating a lack of transparency that "is fueling emotional and irrational decisions" made by schools and conferences.

While schools must report player contracts to the newly created College Sports Commission and the commission gives a broad-brush overview of how much money is spent , there's still very little verified information about how much each school spends on rosters or how much individual athletes make.

Without that transparency, a handful of schools are reportedly spending $50 million on football rosters to stay competitive.

"Those decisions are multiplying like rabbits," Pollard said. "We've created distrust within our industry, (among) our colleagues."

Pollard connects spending for sports to bigger problems ahead for schools

Pollard, whose Big 12 program was a steady presence at both men's and women's March Madness in basketball but rarely broke through in football, cited other research that showed about 16% of public universities lost money in at least five fiscal years between 2014-23. He cited spiraling expenses in sports as part of the reason.

A report this year from the U.S. Government Accountability Office found that 94% of NCAA Division I athletic programs spent more money than they generated in athletics revenue in 2023-24.

"If we're not careful, we're sitting on the next savings and loans crisis in higher education," Pollard said.

A combination of high interest rates and poor management led to the closure of more than 1,000 savings-and-loan institutions around the country in the late 1980s and early '90s.

Leaders from Ivy League, Towson echo concerns about spiraling spending

Other seminar speakers included Robin Harris, the executive director of the Ivy League, and Steve Eigenbrot, the athletic director at Towson, which plays in Division I's smaller-conference Football Championship Subdivision.

Harris lauded the Ivy League's efforts to stay relevant despite not tapping into revenue sharing models that all but about four dozen of the 365 schools in Division I have signed onto.

"The Ivy League remains even more committed to our model in the face of these external pressures," Harris said.

She said in light of the recent announcement of the College Football Playoff's upcoming expansion to 24 teams that "it is time for a meaningful examination of the CFP and FBS football's financial relationship with the NCAA, given the many services the NCAA provides FBS."

FBS is the Football Bowl Subdivision that includes the Power Four and Group of Six conferences — a total of 137 teams.

Eigenbrot questioned the legitimacy of the market college sports has established for its players.

He compared the $45,000 average salary of a player in the NBA's developmental G-League — considered an option for players who don't want to attend college — against the six and seven-figure payments that often go to college players.

"I'm not so sure that if we fast forward three, four, five years down the line, that we haven't done ourselves a disservice relative to the actual name, image and likeness value of an 18- to 22-year-old," Eigenbrot said.

articles.title: El Sporting está muy pendiente de la sanción a Álex Corredera
articles.standfirst: El club asturiano ha recurrido la expulsión del centrocampista en Zubieta para que pueda estar ante Las Palmas
articles.summary: El club asturiano ha recurrido la expulsión del centrocampista en Zubieta para que pueda estar ante Las Palmas
articles.body: El Sporting de Gijón inició este martes la preparación del partido del domingo ante Las Palmas en El Molinón muy pendiente de que se resuelva la sanción a Álex Corredera, expulsado en el último encuentro ante la Real Sociedad B. El club rojiblanco presentó este martes un recurso de apelación ante el Comité de Competición con el objetivo de que se anule la primera tarjeta amarilla del centrocampista, lo que le permitiría evitar el partido de suspensión que debería cumplir frente al conjunto canario. Corredera vio la roja por doble amonestación en el encuentro del sábado en Zubieta después de que la primera tarjeta llegara en el minuto 46 y la segunda en el 80... un partido en el que había abierto el marcador de penalti. La colegiada Marta Huerta de Aza reflejó en el acta que la primera amonestación fue por "derribar de forma temeraria a un contrario" en la disputa del balón, una acción previa al gol del empate local que el club ha revisado en las imágenes de televisión para poder justificar su alegato. El equipo regresó a los entrenamientos en Mareo con una sesión de tarde que combinó trabajo en el gimnasio y en el césped, sin recuperar efectivos respecto a la jornada anterior y con Corredera integrado en el grupo a la espera de conocer la resolución. Si el Comité acepta las alegaciones, el centrocampista estará disponible ante Las Palmas y supondrá una alternativa más para el técnico argentino Nicolás Larcamón, que no podrá contar con Juan Otero, quien cumplirá su segundo partido sanción por increpar al árbitro en el último encuentro disputado en Gijón. Además tampoco estarán los lesionados Konrad, Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García y Manu Rodríguez.

articles.body:
Even though Lane Kiffin is facing criticism after a disappointing season, the LSU head coach is still scoring touchdowns on the recruiting trail. The LSU football program was able to flip a Wake Forest commit, per Rivals.

"Four-Star Safety Keland Shelton Jr. has Flipped his Commitment from Wake Forest to LSU," Hayes Fawcett reported on X, formerly Twitter. "The 6'2 200 (pound) safety had been committed to the Demon Deacons since May."

LSU's newest commit expressed his loyalty to the Tigers, after making the decision. He is a member of the Class of 2027. He also had offers from many other power 4 schools, including Virginia Tech and Tennessee.

"LSU Nation I am coming to give my all! GEAUX TIGERS," Shelton Jr. said, which was reported by Rivals.

LSU is hoping to finish the season on a high note

The LSU football program is 6-4 this season . This is Kiffin's first year in Baton Rouge. His LSU team has lost several close games, which effectively ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff this year.

"Three of LSU's losses (Ole Miss, Kentucky and Texas) were by a combined 10 points, so a different bounce here or there would have changed an outcome, like a receiver not falling on one of Sam Leavitt's interceptions against Texas or a tipped pass ending in a pick against Ole Miss," The Athletic reported.

The team's latest loss was to Texas. LSU was nipped by the Longhorns, 22-21.

"Everything isn't built for the first year when you come in somewhere," Kiffin said after the Texas loss.

It wasn't supposed to be like this though for the Tigers. Kiffin left his last job, Ole Miss, near the end of the 2025 season to come to Baton Rouge. His final Ole Miss team was headed to the CFP, and Kiffin decided to bolt even when he could have led that group to a national championship.

LSU fans expect Kiffin to take the Tigers to the CFP as soon as possible. He will now have to wait until the 2027 season to have another chance.

articles.title: The Revue: Skyfall
articles.summary: This is the end (?) Hold your breath and count to 10.
articles.body:
What's your favorite James Bond movie? Or maybe who's your favorite James Bond?

Personally, I'm a Daniel Craig absolutist. I think some of the early Connery films are pretty good – specifically Goldfinger – and Roger Moore certainly had his moments redefining the character as a Baby Boomer self-parody. But Craig is everything I want Bond to be. Charismatic, brooding, and skilled, with just enough darkness to never betray how jingoist the character is at heart. So maybe it's not a surprise that my favorite Bond film is the one largely viewed as the crowning glory of Craig's 007 run – Skyfall .

If you haven't seen Skyfall and you have even a modicum of interest in the James Bond character, I'd highly recommend it. Without getting too in the weeds of the plot, no film has ever done more to dissect the neuroses and character flaws that would make a person like James Bond the byproduct of a forgone age. Not only that, it leans fully into the anti-social characteristics of James Bond's character. Sure, he's still sleeping with dames and killing for king and country. But it's one of the rare Bonds where you really feel good about everything he's up to.

I also think Skyfall serves as an interesting referendum on the series more than 10 years removed from its production. Craig would go on to make two more tepidly-received Bond movies, and now the franchise is being handed to the capable talents of Denis Villeneuve and Robert Pattinson. Did I mention the Broccoli family, long-time family stewards of the Bond character, are no longer the sole owners and distributors of the franchise? That would be Amazon. Welcome to the 21st century, Mr. Bond.

At no point in the last 25 years has the James Bond character held more cultural sway than just after Skyfall was released. It was praised on not just the merits of a celebrated action blockbuster, but as a critically-acclaimed piece of political espionage craft. Since then, things have felt a little… boring. You know, like a British meal. And when that happens, producers shake things up. Recast. Bring in a new director. The works.

I may be overstating things – after all, it's not like Mizzou fans expected the Tigers to roll into Athens and put one on Georgia – but I'm starting to wonder when Mizzou's Skyfall happened under Eli Drinkwitz. And when might it be time to reimagine what this franchise can look like.

I want to be clear: I'm not advocating Eli Drinkwitz get the axe. If anything, I view Drink as the Broccoli family stand-in of this metaphor. He's been an excellent shepherd of the Mizzou brand since his arrival. He's steadied a program that was still wallowing the shadow of state funding cuts, the 2015 protests, and Gary Pinkel's legacy. He's raised the overall profile of the Tigers from SEC also-rans to perennial Top 25 program. When Drinkwitz took over, a .500 record was seen as the baseline. Ask a Mizzou fan how they'd feel about finishing 6-6 this season. Hope you like seeing a person's blood pressure rise!

But it's clear that Eli Drinkwitz's tenure at Mizzou is currently in something like a creative fallow period. Maybe it's Spectre and we've still got a ways to go before we tweak the right things to get a fresh start. Maybe this season is more of a No Time to Die scenario where we're seeing the quality rebound, but not enough to avoid major changes.

So what does that look like? Is it building next season's offense entirely around Austin Simmons and deprioritizing the outside zone game that allows Mizzou to control games, if not entirely dominate them? Maybe it's admitting that the Chip Lindsey hiring, novel as it seemed, might be a failed experiment. Maybe the changes are smaller, personnel-related tweaks that can be done mostly underneath the hood.

I also think there's a possibility that I'm over-egging the pudding here and that Mizzou hasn't reached a sort of nadir yet. When you look at the amount of players on this team that are eligible to return in 2027, it's hard not to view this season – at least in the hindsight that we have – similar to how we might have viewed 2006. The Tigers were good that year, but were really on the way to building something unforgettable in 2007. The talent is there, after all. The opportunity will be there too, with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 entrants.

But there's a lot of time between now and then. There are still two games to play. And a whole lot of bad things can happen against Kentucky and an Oklahoma team that suddenly remembered how to play football.

So to quote Adele: "Let the sky fall. When it crumbles, we will stand tall and face it all together."

Except, you know… let's avoid any truly "sky is falling" moments if at all possible.

For losing to Georgia and making me think existentially for this column – always hate doing that – Mizzou gets 1/5 martinis . Shaken, not stirred, because James Bond is an alcoholic who doesn't make his drinks correctly.

articles.title: Chennis Berry puts South Carolina State championship success into perspective
articles.summary: The Chennis Berry era at South Carolina State has been an unprecedented success. Heading into the final week of MEAC regular-season play, Berry has yet to lo...
articles.body:
The Chennis Berry era at South Carolina State has been an unprecedented success. Heading into the final week of MEAC regular-season play, Berry has yet to lose a conference game, has won his third straight MEAC championship, and is making his third straight appearance in the Cricket Celebration Bowl.

In recent comments to the media, Berry put his success into perspective, showing reverence to the legendary South Carolina State coaches who came before him. Asked how it feels to join those names with three straight MEAC titles, Berry called them living legends and said he can only be himself.

"Well, you're talking about some living legends, man, so I can't be them. I can only be Chennis Berry."

He said he has the opportunity to write his own story and build his own legacy.

"I get a chance, I got a pen, right? And on this pen, I get a chance to write my own story, build my own legacy. All in all, man, I'm grateful. I stand on the shoulders of giants, man. These are giants, man. I'm not just talking about in HBCU football, I'm talking about nationally."

Berry said he is grateful to be around the history of the program every day, naming Willie Jeffries, Oliver Buddy Pough and Bill Davis.

"I'm grateful to be able to come here every day and just hear those names: Willie Jeffries, Oliver Buddy Pough, Bill Davis. These are shoulders that I get a chance to stand on, man. But it's my opportunity, as the guy that's new here, to find a way to write my own story."

Berry added that the records and championships those coaches built are hard to catch up to, and that his focus stays on the present.

"They got so many records and so many championships, man. It's hard to catch up with them guys, man. So all in all, I just try to be the best I can be on this day. On November the 16th, 2026, I want to be the best Chennis Berry I can be and try to find a way to win this thing."

South Carolina State concludes the regular season hosting Delaware State, then are set to play the SWAC Champions in the Cricket Celebration Bowl.

articles.title: Jamie Carragher calls on Liverpool to back Andoni Iraola in January transfer window
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has called on the Liverpool hierarchy to back manager Andoni Iraola in the upcoming January transfer window, having identified two key positi...
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher is convinced Andoni Iraola must capitalize on the opportunity to utilize the January transfer window to remedy the holes in his Liverpool roster.

What's more, the Anfield icon believes the Reds manager would gain from a decisive win over fierce North West rivals Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Iraola has presided over a consistent beginning to his Liverpool tenure after replacing the dismissed Arne Slot in June, with four senior players acquired for a combined sum exceeding £200 million ($364.2 million).

However, Carragher maintains there are still obvious areas requiring enhancement in the playing squad and that Liverpool must conduct business in the upcoming New Year market.

"I look at this January window for Andoni Iraola and think he needs to go and get the player he wants for the certain position rather than waiting for the summer," he said, via the Liverpool Echo .

"He's only signed a two-year contract, and that was of his own accord which is fine, but that means every transfer window is very important.

"For me, this season for Iraola is about making sure Liverpool are in a position for next season to really challenge for the title. So every transfer window is important.

"The areas on the pitch for Liverpool that still stand out for are the full-back areas. If there's a left-back, they've got to go and do it in January. Or a midfield player, a certain type of midfield player."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Despite sitting fourth in the early Premier League standings, Liverpool have managed just five points from five home fixtures, extending a disappointing top-flight record at Anfield this calendar year.

United currently occupy the relegation zone and last week brought in Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach following Michael Carrick's dismissal, yet they have lost only one of their last seven encounters with Liverpool.

Regarding Iraola, Carragher - speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate - commented: "I think he's made a good start. The one thing lacking is a stellar performance.

"How big is the Manchester United game? For us (as players), obviously it was a big game, but also for the manager really because at the end of the day, if you're the manager of Liverpool, you're going to have to beat your rivals to get over the line in a cup final or a semi-final or win a league.

"And so far, even though the performances were good, I'd say against Manchester City when it was 11 v 11, and Arsenal in the main, both games at home, they lost both of them. Manchester United are coming to town, Liverpool's biggest rivals. I think the manager could do with winning a big home game."

articles.title: Troy Parrott: Republic of Ireland striker caps dream year with two more goals
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott reflects on a transformative 12 months for both club and country after scoring a double in the win against Kosovo.
articles.body:
A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.

His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.

The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.

Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.

The past 12 months have been transformative for Parrott, who also earned a move to Real Betis in the summer after starring for AZ Alkmaar.

He has since scored against Real Madrid and in the Champions League for Betis alongside establishing himself as Republic of Ireland's talisman.

He will carry their hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028, just as his idol and the country's all-time leading scorer Robbie Keane did for many years when he led the line.

While he has taken an arduous route to the top, Parrott is content he is finally fulfilling his potential at club level and on the international stage.

"Growing up watching Robbie Keane, he was the main man and it's always what I wanted to do. I've worked really hard to get here and now I'm in a really good spot," he told RTE.

"Professional football is one of the hardest professions to make it in, so many people want to be a footballer. If I didn't have a stronger mentality, I could have failed.

"Now I am at the level that I always knew I could get to and there are more levels to come. I am really excited for it."

Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo

Republic of Ireland finished their Nations League campaign with two wins, two draws and two defeats from their six games.

The two victories were highlights of what was a testing campaign on and off the pitch because of the decision to go ahead with two games against Israel.

The controversy surrounding the first Israel game in particular - which the Irish ended up winning 3-0 in Debrecen - was difficult for the squad to navigate.

The match looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

Parrott reiterated the point that Dara O'Shea and Nathan Collins made earlier in the week, that the collective group of players are stronger coming out the other side of it all.

"It was very difficult the last camp with all the pressure on us as players, it was a bit of a strange one because no-one has experienced anything like that before - players, staff or the FAI - so it was strange and a bit difficult," he said.

"It was important for us because people had to come out of their shells and give opinions, the quiet ones had to have a voice in the changing room so it was good everyone came together.

"When we played Israel in the away game the performance symbolised everything we went through in the week, we came out and destroyed them."

Republic of Ireland's 'mission' to reach Euro 2028

Republic of Ireland had many "nearly" moments in the group, from the late narrow defeats in Pristina and Linz to the frustration of being pegged back by Israel and Austria in draws when they were ahead.

The pressure was on for them to deliver in their must-win game against Kosovo on Tuesday and they did, comfortably.

Although aided by the red card shown to Kreshnik Hajrizi, Parrott believes they would have still won had Kosovo had 11 men on the pitch and was relieved they could demonstrate again, as they did against Portugal and Hungary last year, that they can win when it matters.

Moving up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 draw should, in theory, present the Irish with a kinder draw for a tournament they are desperate to qualify for, given the Aviva Stadium will host some games.

"We felt and everyone else felt we could have won this group but the most important thing is getting into that pot two. It was a big game for us, it wasn't a nearly game we went out and done it so it's a credit to everyone.

"It's disappointing we didn't win the group because that's what we wanted to do at the start. There's been so many nearly matches where we have nearly won or played well and haven't won and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset no matter what, we had to win.

"It's not guaranteed that we will qualify [for the Euros] so it was important to get pot two to get a better draw and we'll be going to the qualifiers hoping to qualify. A tournament hosted by Ireland without Ireland in it would be heart-breaking, so that's our mission to make sure we're there."

Before attentions turns to Euro 2028 qualifying, Republic of Ireland will take on a League A side over two legs in March's Nations League play-off as they try to reach the top tier for the first time.

Parrott's focus between now and March is clear, getting back to Seville and "putting the ball in the back of the net" for Real Betis as he has done so well for Republic of Ireland in the past year.

articles.title: Craig Bellamy: Wales boss takes belief from Nations League campaign
articles.summary: Wales finished bottom of their Nations League group, but boss Craig Bellamy believes his team showed they belong in the top flight.
articles.body:
Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief.

His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised.

But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom.

Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff.

And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status.

"Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign.

"Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level.

"We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop.

"You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift."

Portugal hold off bold Wales in five-goal thriller

Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated.

Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign.

Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances – combined with sloppy defensive mistakes – meant their results did not match their performances.

And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch.

"If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added.

"I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more.

"I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins.

"But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me."

Wales had the best record of the four teams who finished bottom of their top-flight groups, meaning they have a second chance to avoid relegation in the form of a two-leg play-off in March.

At Friday's draw in Switzerland, Bellamy's side will discover whether they will face Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia-Herzegovina, who beat them in a World Cup play-off earlier this year.

Those teams all finished second in their League B groups and, as the League A team, Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.

"Going into the next one, we have to be in this group," said Bellamy. "If we want to develop as a football nation and keep going forward, we have to be playing against the best teams. It's only going to improve you.

"I know we can go back to League B... It's about playing the best teams. That's how we're going to get better. I honestly believe it."

Bellamy, who has a contract running to 2028, said: "I won't be here for the next Nations League. I won't be the manager then. So I'm doing it for the next one, but I'm also doing it for the players.

"We've got to. That's how we're going to be the best version of us and keep improving."

articles.title: Nations League: Belief and bench help Northern Ireland to League A promotion
articles.summary: Manager Michael O'Neill hails the belief shown by his side after they come from behind against Hungary to earn the draw required for promotion to Nations League A.
articles.body:
After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Puskas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit - on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game - displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point from a 1-1 draw in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.

"We went behind tonight and it was difficult, you know? Big stadium, big atmosphere, but we came out and played well in the second half and got what we needed from the game," said the manager.

"Those are things that I'm very pleased that are in this squad at such a young age. The technical side of the game we'll always look to improve on, but in terms of the physical, the tactical and the mental side of a game, we're very far ahead of where I thought we would be at this time."

Northern Ireland draw with Hungary to seal Nations League promotion

Watch: Devenny the hero as NI earn promotion

Hungary enjoyed more than 70% possession in the first half, and they could have been further than a goal ahead with Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai striking the base of the post after only five minutes.

O'Neill made his first change at half-time, bringing on veteran striker Josh Magennis, while Kieran Morrison, Brodie Spencer and Paul Smyth all followed in the second half.

Magennis and Morrison made a real impact before the equaliser, but it was the belief shown by all involved that O'Neill felt was key to the turnaround.

"I felt in the first half from where I was seeing the game, we just looked a little bit leggy which is natural," added O'Neill.

"I just felt we needed that freshness at the right points in the game that helped us, but it was the belief that we could get back into the game, and the belief that we could see the game out.

"I think we showed a lot of attributes that are in this squad at this moment in time and certainly in the second half that was that was the case."

For all the plaudits earned by this team who conceded just one goal in six games while picking up 12 points, among the most impressive aspects of the campaign has been who they have had to do without.

Talismanic Liverpool defender Conor Bradley has not played for this side in over 12 months through injury.

Ali McCann is another who missed both 2026 Nations League windows, while influential defender Daniel Ballard featured only in the first game in Georgia before a hamstring injury.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill was forced to pull out of the November squad through injury at a time when he would perhaps have been the most natural replacement for Jamie Donley after the striker picked up a second booking against Ukraine last week and had to miss the finale through suspension.

Having taken over an ageing squad four years ago, O'Neill has rebuilt his playing panel with a group that feels as if it is getting deeper with each international window.

"The encouraging thing is we have players on the outside - we've Bradley to come back in, Ballard to come back in, Ali McCann, young Ceadach, Eoin Toal," added the former Stoke City and Blackburn Rovers boss.

"We have good competition for places now. We're going to need that competition, and some players are going to miss out, but we are building depth to the squad that will help us going forward."

Come the next Nations League, that will be all the way into the uncharted territory of the top tier.

articles.title: Show de Julián, Nico Paz y Mastantuono, con tres dobletes en la paliza de Argentina
articles.standfirst: Alexis Mac Allister redondeó el 7-0 en el amistoso ante Costa Rica
articles.summary: Mastantuono y Alexis redondearon el 'set' en el amistoso ante Costa Rica
articles.body: Argentina se divirtió en la madrugada española ante una Costa Rica (sin el meta Keylor Navas) que fue un juguete en pies argentinos. Un 7-0 que se resume en tres dobletes: Julián Álvarez y Nico Paz, sólo en los primeros 45 minutos, pues ambos fueron cambiados en el descanso; y Mastantuono, sólo en la segunda parte, pues salió en el 45'. El 7-0 se completó con tanto de Alexis Mac Allister. Viendo el partido de esta noche, quedan claras dos cosas en esta Argentina posMessi: Nico Paz es el indiscutible nuevo número 10 de la Albiceleste (use o no use, como hoy, el dorsal en la espalda); y Julián Álvarez debe seguir siendo la referencia arriba, como lo atestiguan sus 19 goles en 64 partidos con la camiseta de su país. El rojiblanco ha marcado tres goles en los dos amistosos de esta 'ventana' y se empieza a acercar al 'prime' que le exige el Atlético. Por su parte, lo de Nico Paz es de escándalo. La 10 aún no la lleva nadie en la era posMessi (aunque en los torneos FIFA sí debe portarla alguien), pero su categoría y clase le hacen merecedor del peso de llevar el número del crack Lionel. Esta noche marcó un doblete de crack. El segundo gol, tras deshacerse de varios rivales, y meter un derechazo (su pierna mala) escalofriante. Es el quinto gol de NP tras el Mundial después de los logrados ante Bolivia, Burkina y Benin. Los dos dobletes de Nico y Julián pusieron el 4-0 en el descanso, junto a un tiro al palo de Prestianni y una buena parada del 'Dibu' Martínez, cuando apenas Costa Rica perdía 1-0. Lo único malo de este nuevo amistoso albiceleste fue, de nuevo, la flojísima entrada en el Mario Kempes, que registró poco menos de media entrada con alguna tribuna vacía, cosa que ya había ocurrido en el partido ante Uruguay (1-2) en La Bombonera de Buenos Aires. La segunda parte, ya sin Julián ni Nico, tenía el aliciente de la entrada de Mastantuono, que apenas tardó tres minutos en poner el 5-0 con una buena jugada por la derecha. El jugador cedido por el Real Madrid se unía así a la fiesta con este gol y uno último, que hacía el 7-0, en los últimos minutos, ratificando que es un gran suplente de Nico Paz. Poco más en una segunda parte con muchos cambios en la que Argentina se la tomó a otro ritmo, pese al sexto gol de Mac Allister que antecedía al mencionado 7-0 que cerraba el marcador. El rojiblanco Giuliano Simeone salió en el minuto 71' en lugar de Prestianni. Y así acabó este entrenamiento-amistoso. Buen segundo partido del renovado Scaloni en la era posMessi tras la derrota ante Uruguay de la semana pasada.

images.caption: Julián celebra el doblete.
Nico Paz, en el choque ante Costa Rica.

articles.title: Dante Moore Injury Update, Oregon QB's Status for Potential CFP Run Updated by Dan Lanning
articles.summary: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning essentially confirmed on Tuesday that quarterback Dante Moore's season is over as he recovers from a concussion suffered during a Sept. 26 matchup against USC.
articles.body:
Oregon head coach Dan Lanning essentially confirmed on Tuesday that quarterback Dante Moore's season is over as he recovers from a concussion suffered during a Sept. 26 matchup against USC.

"Yeah, I don't think we're going to be able to get Dante back. Again, like I said, the ball's not really in his court. You're not in charge of the medical advice when it comes to that," Lanning said during an appearance on the "Bussin' with the Boys" podcast (2:08:48 mark). "Dante's going to be able to play football again. I know that; I feel very confident about it. He's practicing with us right now; we get the best scout team look in America. He's chopping us up over there on the defensive side. He's an unbelievable teammate, and his leadership has shown up. But I don't anticipate us getting to see Dante out there for us again this year."

Lanning previously told reporters in October that Moore was unlikely to return this season and hadn't been medically cleared.

"If it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would be out there playing for the guys," he said on Oct. 26. "This isn't a selfish decision on Dante's part, saying, 'I don't want to come back, the season doesn't look the way I want it to look.' That's not at all what this is."

Moore was hit late by USC linebacker Desman Stephens II during the 41-27 win. The Ducks then lost two of their next three games before pulling off wins over Northwestern, Ohio State and Michigan. While the Ducks aren't currently ranked, wins over Michigan State and Washington could have them in the running for an appearance in the Big Ten title game if either UCLA or Indiana slips up down the stretch.

And at the very least, the College Football Playoff Committee would have to give some weight to a potential five-game winning streak. Either way, it doesn't sound like Moore would be available to the team were they to reach the CFP.

articles.title: Valverde redondea con un buen tanto la 'Manita' de la Uruguay de Forlán
articles.standfirst: La Celeste venció ante la República Dominicana... y reservando a Fede
articles.summary: La Celeste venció ante la República Dominicana... y reservando a Fede
articles.body: Fede Valverde, con un buen disparo desde fuera del área, redondeó la 'Manita' que Uruguay le ha metido a Dominicana, en un amistoso en Montevideo en el que Fede jugó sólo la última media hora siendo reservado por Forlán. Fede llega así a los 10 goles con la Celeste. Diego Forlán se está ganando, triunfo a triunfo, el derecho de permanecer como seleccionador de Uruguay, después de la contundente derrota de esta noche (3-0) ante la República Dominicana, con Mariano como delantero centro, en un amistoso disputado en el Estadio Centenario de Montevideo, la capital uruguaya. Los goles de Rodrigo Aguirre, en la primera parte, Valdéz, en propia puerta, y Nico de la Cruz, de penalti, estos dos en la segunda parte, pusieron la ventaja de una Uruguay que jugó en su once inicial sin Federico Valverde. El madridista entró en el minuto 62 sustituyendo a Rodrigo Salazar como centrocampista y con su participación se fabricaron el segundo y el tercer gol de la Celeste. Con este triunfo, con la portería a cero por primera vez, Diego Forlán completa una ventana perfecta, ya que le ganó a Argentina en la Bombonera, y ahora esta goleada ante República Dominicana. En la pasada ventana de octubre- noviembre, el seleccionador Forlán dirigió a la Celeste ante Japón (derrota 3-1), y ganó los amistosos ante Corea (1-4) y ante la India (1-6). Un balance más que positivo para que la AUF decida su nuevo seleccionador tras las elecciones que vendrán en la Federación próximamente. Forlán, por el momento, está asegurado para ser el seleccionador Sub 20 que participará en el sudamericano de la categoría a principios de año.
